:::{#thm-kl-divergence-nonnegative}
#### Gibbs' inequality: the divergence is nonnegative

For $p$ and $q$ as in @thm-kl-divergence-discrete,
the [KL divergence](#def-kl-divergence) satisfies

$$\kldivf{p}{q} \ge 0,$$

with $\kldivf{p}{q} = 0$ exactly when $p_k = q_k$ for every $k$.
The [logarithm](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm) is natural here.
Any other logarithm multiplies the divergence by a positive number.

:::

::: proof

Every [sum](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-summation) below runs over the $k$ with $p_k > 0$.
By @thm-kl-divergence-discrete,
$\kldivf{p}{q} = \sum_k p_k \log \frac{p_k}{q_k}
= -\sum_k p_k \log \frac{q_k}{p_k}$.

By [the bound on the logarithm](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/optimization-convexity.html#cor-log-below-tangent),
$\log t \le t - 1$ for every $t > 0$,
with equality exactly when $t = 1$.
Take $t = q_k / p_k$,
and multiply by $p_k > 0$:

$$p_k \log \frac{q_k}{p_k} \le q_k - p_k,$$

with equality exactly when $q_k = p_k$.
Summing over $k$ gives

$$
\ba
\sum_k p_k \log \frac{q_k}{p_k}
&\le \sum_k q_k - \sum_k p_k && \text{(sum the bound over } k \text{)} \\
&= \sum_k q_k - 1 && \text{(} p \text{ sums to one)} \\
&\le 0. && \text{(} q \text{ sums to at most one)}
\ea
$$

Hence $\kldivf{p}{q} = -\sum_k p_k \log \frac{q_k}{p_k} \ge 0$.

Suppose $\kldivf{p}{q} = 0$.
Then both relations above hold with equality.
Equality in the first forces $q_k = p_k$ whenever $p_k > 0$.
Equality in the second then gives $\sum_k q_k = 1$,
so $q_k = 0$ whenever $p_k = 0$.
Hence $q_k = p_k$ for every $k$.
Conversely, if $q_k = p_k$ for every $k$,
every [term](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-sums.html#def-term) $p_k \log \frac{p_k}{q_k}$ is $0$.

:::
